name: Ceftriaxone
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.dose: 1 to 2 g IV or IM once daily (or divided twice daily); maximum 4 g/day
1 g IV once, 30 minutes to 2 hours before surgery

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Calcium-containing IV solutions (Ringer's, Hartmann's, parenteral nutrition)
key_interactions.effect: Ceftriaxone-calcium precipitates; fatal lung and kidney deposits in neonates (label).
key_interactions.action: Never mix or give together; neonates: contraindicated; others: give sequentially with line flushes.

serious: Ceftriaxone-calcium precipitation (gallbladder, kidney; lung in neonates)
Encephalopathy, seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus (severe kidney impairment)

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to ceftriaxone or other cephalosporins
Premature neonates up to 41 weeks postmenstrual age; hyperbilirubinemic neonates
Neonates (28 days or younger) needing calcium-containing IV solutions
monitoring: Neurologic status in severe kidney impairment
Signs of biliary or urinary precipitation

pk.half_life_eskd: About 14.7 hours on hemodialysis; 15.7 hours at CrCl 5–15 (label Table 4)
pk.metabolism: Not metabolized; biliary portion inactivated in gut
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 33% to 67% unchanged in urine; rest in bile
